newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Italy's Prodi says no set date for ERM re-entry.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi says no set date for ERM re-entry.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Friday there was no set date for the lira's re-entry into the European exchange rate mechanism, but that Italy was likely to apply for re-entry this year.

"There is no precise date," Prodi told Reuters during a meeting of eastern and central European heads of governments in southern Austria. "In due time we shall start the process of application for re-entry in the ERM."
Asked whether this would happen before the end of the year, Prodi added "I guess so."
Prodi added his government was working hard on qualifying for entry into Europe's planned monetary union by 1999. "We are concentrating all our energies in that direction," he said.

Italy was forced to leave the exchange rate mechanism (ERM) amid a wave of currency turmoil in 1992. The country needs to get back into the ERM this year if it wants to stand a chance at qualifying for EMU membership in time.

The government has proposed a tough 62.5 trillion lire austerity budget, aimed at slashing Italy's ballooning public debt, which is running at some 123 percent of gross domestic product this year. The budget is due to be voted on by parliament next week.
Italian Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco said late Thursday that Italy expected to return the lira to the ERM by the end of November, with 1,000-1,050 per mark seen as the best rate.
Visco said "Within this month we must enter the (exchange rate mechanism)."

"I think a balanced solution with the mark between 1,000 and 1,050 lire would be more than reasonable, especially as we are in a situation in which we still have a little potential competitive advantage," he said.
